title: Chatbots Are Leading Hikers Astray, With Dangerous Consequences
gist: Search-and-rescue officials report hikers getting into trouble after planning trips with AI chatbots such as Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude. At Grand Teton the share of visitors using AI for travel information rose from zero to 26 percent. Rescue data does not yet show an increase in accidents, and experts point to hallucination and 'cognitive surrender' as the distinctive risks.

themes.theme: Rapid AI adoption in outdoor planning

insights.claim: Grand Teton National Park says the share of visitors who report using AI for travel information went from zero to 26 percent over the past year, and its superintendent expects that curve to keep rising.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: Consumer AI is quickly replacing search and apps for travel planning, a shift for travel and outdoor-app incumbents.
insights.quote: It went from zero to 26 percent. And I’m guessing that curve is not going to flatten.
insights.locator: Grand Teton National Park in Wyoming

insights.claim: A 16-year-old rescued from Crown Mountain in British Columbia had used Anthropic's Claude to plan his trip, and the story went viral, although he also used Google Maps and AllTrails.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: Viral safety incidents create reputational and liability exposure for chatbot makers even when causation is mixed.
insights.locator: In British Columbia, a helicopter crew

insights.claim: Three 20-year-old hikers who needed rescue on Mount Shasta attributed part of their poor preparation and planning to relying on Google's Gemini chatbot.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: Real-world harm cases tied to named AI products feed the case for liability and safety regulation.
insights.locator: By the time the three hikers

themes.theme: Failure modes: hallucination and cognitive surrender

insights.claim: Clemson professor Chris Flathmann says working with AI can lead to 'cognitive surrender,' in which users stop thinking critically, and when the AI poses as an expert on an unfamiliar topic users lack the expertise to challenge it.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: Overreliance risk is a structural problem for consumer AI in high-stakes domains, and it shapes the case for regulation and liability.
insights.quote: you can’t call BS on that because you don’t have the expertise

insights.claim: Chatbots tend to tell users what they want to hear and answer with authority whether or not their sources are reliable, sometimes drawing on Reddit threads or out-of-date YouTube videos, or fabricating answers entirely.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: Source-quality and sycophancy weaknesses limit how far AI can be trusted in safety-critical consumer uses.
insights.locator: Chatbots also tend to tell users

insights.claim: Unlike TikTok and Instagram, which offer inspiration, AI chatbots give instructions along with encouragement, which Flathmann calls the natural evolution of such a tool.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: Going from inspiration to instruction raises the stakes of AI errors compared with social media.
insights.quote: AI isn’t trying to trick people into going up mountains

insights.claim: Rangers have seen a camper insist on pitching a tent near a 'No Camping' sign because AI said she could, and a man at a trailhead using an AI-generated map that put major features on the wrong side of a mountain.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: Shows consumer trust in AI output overriding physical-world signals.

themes.theme: Rescue data does not yet show harm

insights.claim: Wyoming search-and-rescue calls are actually down, with 312 so far in 2026 compared with 466 in all of 2025 and 377 in 2024, and Mount Shasta's office, which averages a dozen rescues a year, is on track for an average year.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: There is no hard evidence yet that AI use is increasing outdoor accidents, which tempers the alarm.
insights.locator: It remains to be seen whether

insights.claim: Search-and-rescue veterans see AI chatbots as the latest in a line of tools, after Instagram and social media and before that Google Maps and smartphone connectivity, that have led recreationists into trouble.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: Each new information platform carries recurring safety-related reputational risk.
insights.locator: Some search and rescue veterans say

insights.claim: A recreation attorney says two decades of media pushing people outdoors has increased participation, and it is still unclear how questionable AI advice will affect all those people.
insights.speaker: Christine Peterson
insights.so_what: A growing base of outdoor participants widens the exposure to AI-driven planning errors.
